Project.How do you plan to prepare the dataset:
The Filecoin data preparation process begins when a user initiates a storage deal through client tools such as Lotus or Fuhon, packaging the raw data into a CAR file for transmission.  
The data is then sent to a miner, who verifies its integrity (via root CID comparison) and assigns it to an appropriate sector for preprocessing.  
Next comes the "Sealing" process, which consists of multiple stages: PreCommit1 encodes the data and generates the CommD, while PreCommit2 performs cryptographic computations to produce CommR and CommC.  
In the Seal Commit phase, the miner uses GPU or specialized hardware to generate zero-knowledge proofs, completing the verifiable encapsulation of the data replica.  
After sealing, the miner submits the PreCommit and Commit proofs to the Filecoin blockchain using node software like Lotus, awaiting on-chain verification.  
Once verified, the sector is activated and begins periodically submitting Proof-of-Spacetime (PoSt) to continuously prove the data is being stored.  
The entire process relies on Filecoin's Proof-of-Replication (PoRep) and Proof-of-Spacetime (PoSt) mechanisms to ensure data is stored reliably and verifiably across the network.
